pr_title: Add warnings and fallbacks for particles sub emitters when using the GL Compatibility rendering backend
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/78483

This PR does the following:
1. Adds a configuration warning when assigning a subemitter to a Particles node (both 2D and 3D)
2. Adds a printed warning when enabling a subemitters in the ParticleProcessMaterial
3. Avoids inserting subemitter related code into ParticlesProcessMaterial shader
4. Adds fallbacks when subemitter functionality is used in a shader
5. Cleans up error messages relating to GL Compatibility renderer (many of these should have been exposed to toasts, and many also referenced OpenGL 2 or 3)
pr_comments: Thanks! I applied your suggested changes

This really needs more then a warning. 
What stops the feature from being implemented in compatibility mode? 
Even if it's slow and warns us it's still better then crashing or doing nothing

> This really needs more then a warning. 

What do you suggest? In the past we hid unsupported features, but it ended up being really confusing for users and detrimental to the user experience. 


> What stops the feature from being implemented in compatibility mode? Even if it's slow and warns us it's still better then crashing or doing nothing

The fact that we want the GL Compatibility renderer to target low end devices. If we implemented it, it would likely only be supported on high end devices, which defeats the point of having a low end focussed renderer. It is extremely important to us to be able to deliver something that is functional for users who don't have new/expensive devices

> > This really needs more then a warning.
> 
> What do you suggest? In the past we hid unsupported features, but it ended up being really confusing for users and detrimental to the user experience.

Most software would just grey out the text of functionality that can't be used. It is also a big problem with the mobile renderer and not knowing what is and isn't supported. I agree that hiding unusable options is a bad idea but having the text greyed out or some other color would go a long way toward resolving these issues.

> Most software would just grey out the text of functionality that can't be used. It is also a big problem with the mobile renderer and not knowing what is and isn't supported. I agree that hiding unusable options is a bad idea but having the text greyed out or some other color would go a long way toward resolving these issues.

I agree. We also need the ability to turn off the feature if you enabled it while using a different backend. That was a common problem in 3.x, people would turn on a feature, switch to GLES2, then get error spam with no ability to turn off the feature
Okay, updated again with more suggested changes. Should be fine to merge once CI passes

What about greying it out and using a popup text on hover? 

Something like...
`This is not supported in compatibility mode please switch to mobile or forward+ to use this feature`
